title: Crop Insurance Underwriting Rule: One Policy Record per Crop, County and Crop Year
content:
**Clause.** All of a member's acreage of one crop in one county for one crop year is insured under a single policy record, at one plan and coverage level; a second record for the same crop, county and crop year is never opened. Acreage of the same crop in another county is a separate record and may carry a different coverage level. Enterprise units combine all of the crop's acreage in the county and require planting in at least the number of sections the product sets for enterprise units.

The clause governs every Crop Insurance application and every acreage report: whatever acres of the crop the member plants in the county that crop year, they are reported to and insured under that one record.

## What makes two records "the same"

The test is made on the association's own policy records, before an application is registered, not on what the member says about them. An existing record counts as the one record when all four of the following match the application:

1. the same member;
2. the same crop;
3. the same county;
4. the same crop year;

and the existing record stands in **applied** or **active** status.

| Existing record found (hypothetical) | Status | A second record for this crop, county and crop year |
|---|---|---|
| Same member, crop, county and crop year | applied | never opened |
| Same member, crop, county and crop year | active | never opened |
| Same member, crop, county and crop year | cancelled, terminated or expired | not counted as the one record |
| Same member, crop and crop year, another county | any | not the same record; the other county is a separate record |
| Same member, county and crop year, another crop | any | not the same record |
| Same member, crop and county, another crop year | any | not the same record |

## Points of judgement

- *One plan and coverage level per record.* Because all of the crop's acreage in the county is under one record, all of it carries the same plan and coverage level. A member cannot insure part of the county's corn at one level and the rest at another.
- *Two counties, two levels.* Corn in one county may be insured at Revenue Protection 80% Coverage while corn in a neighbouring county is insured at Revenue Protection 70% Coverage: they are separate records.
- *Enterprise units.* An enterprise unit takes in all of the crop's acreage in the county, and the crop must be planted in at least as many sections as the product's enterprise-unit section figure for the plan and coverage level.
